nrr:applicabilityConditions.reaction: hydroboration of terminal alkynes and alkenes with pinacolborane in toluene (and diglyme), BH3 at 20 mol %

@graph.nrr:outcomeSummary: Alkyne: 0.3 mM/s and 4 % at 60 °C against 9.6 mM/s and 87 % for free BH3; 50 % at 80 °C and 94 % at 100 °C. Alkene: 0.02 mM/s and 3 % at 60 °C against 1.8 mM/s and >95 %; complete at 80 and 100 °C. HBpin alone decomposes to BH3 from 80 °C.

nrr:evidence.label: Abstract
nrr:evidence.quote: Kinetic analyses showed that TMEDA inhibition is only applicable below 60 °C and that other amine traps are likewise ineffective.

nrr:evidence.label: Conclusion
nrr:evidence.quote: Application of the TMEDA inhibition test, to identify hidden BH3 catalysis, was found to be unsuitable above 60 °C when using a one-to-one loading of TMEDA to 'catalyst'. Higher loading of TMEDA, with respect to catalyst, offered increased inhibition of BH3 catalysis but did not give complete inhibition of catalysis; thus, false negatives remain possible. Reaction at temperatures of >=80 °C will generate BH3 by thermal decomposition of HBpin, and therefore will always be susceptible to hidden BH3 catalysis.

@graph.nrr:note: What is refuted is the inference 'no inhibition, therefore true catalysis' above 60 °C, not the existence of hidden catalysis. The record keeps the test valid at or below 60 °C.
@graph.nrr:informativenessReason: an affirmative refutation is judged on the refuting analysis, not on the controls of the run it refutes

@graph.nrr:question: At what temperature does pinacolborane alone decompose to BH3?

nrr:effect.metric: lowest temperature at which Et3N.BH3 is observed by 11B NMR after 20 h

negative.label: distilled HBpin with Et3N at room temperature, 60 and 70 °C for 20 h

nrr:evidence.label: SI S3.5 and Figure S5
nrr:evidence.quote: no decomposition of distilled HBpin with Et3N after 20 h at room temperature, 60 or 70 °C; Et3N.BH3 observed after 20 h at 80 °C; other decomposition products at 90 and 100 °C (SI S3.5, Figure S5); commercial HBpin contains 0.1 to 1.5 percent triethylamine and often trace BH3
